messages:
morgan: Heads-up — we're targeting a cutover at 20:00 UTC (≈1h from now). Two PRs need final signoff before the window: PR #7421 (kv-cache hotfix) and PR #7430 (canary routing tweak). We need two approvals total across these PRs before cutoff. Can people take a quick look? :eyes:

sam: I can take #7421 now, running the e2e locally. If green I'll drop an LGTM.

kia: I started a security pass on #7421, a couple small comments about header validation. Won't block but want to add notes, will push comments in ~8m.

alex: I can be second approver for either PR after comments are addressed. ping me when ready.

morgan: Thanks. Important: if we don't reach two approvals by 20:00 UTC we will hold the cutover and roll the changes into the next window. Please call it out if you can't review.

sam: e2e passed locally for #7421, unit checks + lint ✅. Leaving an inline review now.

deploy-bot: preflight: PR 7421 - build passed; integration smoke: passed; canary image built (sha: abc123).

kia: left two comments on input sanitization, small nit + suggestion. I'll approve after the one-line fix.

sam: fixing the nit in a tiny patch, will push in 3m.

morgan: Helpful to include the merge commands for whoever merges:
```
# merge candidate after 2x LGTM and green CI
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git merge --no-ff pr/7421
./scripts/deploy-candidate.sh --tag rc-7421
```

kia: pushed fix and requested re-review.

sam: re-reviewed, looks good. LGTM from me. :thumbsup:

alex: Giving second approval for #7421 now. LGTM.

morgan: Awesome — that's 2x for #7421. Who's taking #7430? We still want that in this window but it's not blocking if it misses it.

alex: I'll glance at #7430 — looks small, should be quick. If anything blocks I'll shout.

deploy-bot: deploy candidate for RC created: rc-7421-1981234567. All checks green.

morgan: OK team — merging #7421 in 10m unless anyone objects. If you want to hold we can pause.

kia: fine to merge from security side.

sam: good to go.

morgan: merging now, will watch post-deploy metrics and the canary. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
